scenarios.title: Create book with all required fields
scenarios.then: 201 Created response containing the new book with id 1

scenarios.title: Create book missing required field (title)
scenarios.then: 400 Bad Request with error message about missing title

scenarios.title: Update book with invalid JSON body
scenarios.then: 400 Bad Request with error message about invalid JSON

scenarios.title: Query with unknown parameter
scenarios.given: Book with id=1 exists from previous create; PORT=8000
scenarios.then: 400 Bad Request with error about unknown query parameter

logic: Use an in-memory dict `books = {}` mapping id -> book dict. Book fields: id (int), title (str, required), author (str, required), isbn (str, required), synopsis (str, optional, default "").
On POST /books: extract id from path (must be int), validate required fields are present and non-empty strings, assign next sequential id, store book, return 201 with the new book.
On GET /books/{id}: look up by id; if not found return 404.

On PUT /books/{id}: validate JSON body is a dict; extract title, author, isbn, synopsis; update only provided fields (or all if missing); ensure required fields are non-empty strings; return 200 with updated book or 404 if id not found.
On GET /books: return list of all books sorted by id. Support query params: id=, title=..., author=..., isbn=..., synopsis=..., q=... (case-insensitive, all-or-nothing match).
Unknown query parameter in GET /books: collect all query keys; if any key not in {id, title, author, isbn, synopsis, q} return 400 with error about unknown param.
Invalid JSON body in PUT: try json.loads; if fails return 400 with error about invalid JSON.
